verses.1:1: The words of the Preacher, son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: "Vanity of vanities," said the Preacher, "vanity of vanities; all things are vanity."
verses.1:3: What advantage has a man in all his toil in which he toils under the sun?
verses.1:4: A generation departs and a generation comes, and the earth stands forever.
verses.1:5: And the sun rises and the sun goes down, and draws toward its place.
verses.1:6: Rising there, it goes toward the south and circles toward the north; circling round and round, the wind goes, and upon its circuits the wind returns.
verses.1:7: All the streams go into the sea, and the sea will not be filled; to the place where the streams go, there they return to go again.
verses.1:8: All words are wearisome; a man will not be able to speak, and the eye will not be satisfied with seeing, nor will the ear be filled from hearing.
verses.1:9: What is that which has been? It is the very thing that will be. And what is that which has been done? It is the very thing that will be done. And there is nothing fresh under the sun.
verses.1:10: He who speaks and says, "Behold, this is new!"—it has already been in the ages that came before us.
verses.1:11: There is no remembrance of the former ones, nor indeed of the latter ones that come to be; there will be no remembrance of them among those who shall come at the last.
verses.1:12: I, the Preacher, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: And I gave my heart to search out and to examine by wisdom concerning all things that come to pass under heaven; for an evil preoccupation God has given to the sons of men, to be preoccupied with it.
verses.1:14: I saw all the works that have been done under the sun, and behold, all things are vanity and a purpose of spirit.
verses.1:15: That which is crooked will not be able to be set in order, and that which is lacking will not be able to be numbered.
verses.1:16: I spoke in my heart, saying, "Behold, I have grown great, and I have increased wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem."
verses.1:17: And my heart saw many things, wisdom and knowledge; and I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge; parables and understanding I came to know. For indeed this also is a purpose of spirit.
verses.1:18: For in an abundance of wisdom there is an abundance of knowledge, and he who adds knowledge will add pain.
verses.2:1: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with gladness, and look upon good." And behold, this also is vanity.
verses.2:2: To laughter I said, "Madness!" and to gladness, "What is this that you do?"
verses.2:3: And I examined whether my heart would draw my flesh like wine—while my heart guided me in wisdom—and to lay hold upon gladness, until I might see what is good for the sons of men, which they should do under the sun for the number of the days of their life.
verses.2:4: I made my work great; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
verses.2:5: I made for myself gardens and orchards, and I planted in them every tree of fruit.
verses.2:6: I made for myself pools of water, to water from them a flourishing grove.
verses.2:7: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants born in my house belonged to me; indeed, a great possession of herds and flocks became mine, beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem.
verses.2:8: I gathered for myself both silver and gold, and the special treasures of kings and of the provinces; I procured for myself male singers and female singers, the delights of the sons of men, a male cupbearer and female cupbearers.
verses.2:9: And I grew great and increased beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem; moreover, my wisdom stood by me.
verses.2:10: And all that my eyes requested I did not withhold from them; I did not keep back my heart from any of my gladness, for my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this became my portion from all my toil.
verses.2:11: Then I looked upon all my works which my hands had made, and upon the toil in which I had toiled to perform them; and behold, all things were vanity and a purpose of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun.
verses.2:12: And I looked to behold wisdom and madness and folly; for who is the man who will come after counsel, in all that he has done with it?
verses.2:13: And I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as the advantage of light over darkness.
verses.2:14: The wise man's eyes are in his head, while the fool walks in darkness; yet I also knew that one event will befall them all.
verses.2:15: And I said in my heart, "As the event of the fool, even to me also it will befall me; and why then did I become wise?" I spoke exceedingly in my heart that this also is vanity, because the fool speaks out of abundance.
verses.2:16: For there is no remembrance of the wise man with the fool forever, since already in the coming days all things have been forgotten; and how shall the wise man die along with the fool?
verses.2:17: Therefore I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous upon me; for all things are vanity and a purpose of spirit.
verses.2:18: And I hated all my toil at which I labor under the sun, because I leave it to the man who comes after me.
verses.2:19: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool, and whether he will have dominion over all my toil in which I have toiled and acted wisely under the sun? This also is vanity.
verses.2:20: So I turned to cause my heart to renounce all my toil in which I had toiled under the sun.
verses.2:21: For there is a man whose toil is in wisdom and in knowledge and in courage, yet to a man who has not toiled in it he will give his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.2:22: For it comes to pass for a man in all his toil and in the purpose of his heart with which he toils under the sun.
verses.2:23: For all his days are of pains, and his preoccupation is of anger; indeed, even in the night his heart does not sleep. This also is vanity.
verses.2:24: There is no good for a man that he should eat and drink and show his soul good in his toil; this also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.2:25: For who shall eat and who shall drink apart from Him?
verses.2:26: For to the man who is good before His face He has given wisdom and knowledge and gladness; but to the one who sins He has given preoccupation, to add and to gather, that he may give to the one who is good before the face of God. For this also is vanity and a purpose of spirit.
verses.3:1: For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven.
verses.3:2: A season to give birth and a season to die; a season to plant and a season to pluck up what has been planted;
verses.3:3: A season to slay and a season to heal; a season to tear down and a season to build;
verses.3:4: A season to weep and a season to laugh; a season to mourn and a season to dance;
verses.3:5: A season to cast stones and a season to gather stones; a season to embrace and a season to keep far from embracing;
verses.3:6: A season to seek and a season to lose; a season to keep and a season to cast away;
verses.3:7: A season to rend and a season to sew; a season to keep silent and a season to speak;
verses.3:8: A season to love and a season to hate; a season of war and a season of peace.
verses.3:9: What advantage has the worker in those things in which he toils?
verses.3:10: I saw all the preoccupation which God has given to the sons of men, to be preoccupied with it.
verses.3:11: All things that He has made are beautiful in their season; moreover, He has put all eternity in their heart, so that man may not find out the work which God has wrought from the beginning even to the end.
verses.3:12: I perceived that there is no good among them, except to be glad and to do good in his life.
verses.3:13: And indeed, every man who shall eat and drink and see good in all his toil—this is a gift of God.
verses.3:14: I knew that all things that God has done, they shall be forever; to it nothing can be added, and from it nothing can be taken away; and God has done it so that they should fear before His face.
verses.3:15: That which has been already is, and all that is to come has already been; and God will seek out the one who is pursued.
verses.3:16: And furthermore I saw under the sun the place of judgment—there was the ungodly one; and the place of the righteous—there was the godly one.
verses.3:17: And I said in my heart, "God will judge both the righteous and the ungodly, for there is a season for every matter and for every work."
verses.3:18: And I said in my heart concerning the speech of the sons of man, that God will discern them, and to show that they themselves are beasts.
verses.3:19: And indeed for them, is not the event of the sons of man also the event of the beast? One event is theirs: as the death of the one, so is the death of the other, and there is one spirit for all. And what advantage has man over the beast? Nothing, for all things are vanity.
verses.3:20: All things go to one place; all things came from the dust, and all things shall return to the dust.
verses.3:21: And who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it ascends upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it descends downward into the earth?
verses.3:22: And I saw that there is no good thing except that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what will come to pass after him?
verses.4:1: And I turned again and saw all the oppressions that take place under the sun; behold, the tear of those who are oppressed, and there is no one to comfort them; and from the hand of those who oppress them is power, and there is no one to comfort them.
verses.4:2: And I praised all the dead who have already died more than the living, as many as still live until now.
verses.4:3: And better than both of these is the one who has not yet come into being, who has not seen all the evil work that has been done under the sun.
verses.4:4: And I saw all the toil and all the prowess of the work, that it is jealousy for a man from his companion; this also is vanity and an inclination of spirit.
verses.4:5: The fool clasps his hands together and devours his own flesh.
verses.4:6: Better is a handful of rest than two handfuls of toil and inclination of spirit.
verses.4:7: And I turned again and saw vanity under the sun.
verses.4:8: There is one alone, and there is no second; indeed, he has neither son nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his toil, nor is his eye satisfied with wealth. "And for whom do I toil and deprive my soul of goodness?" This also is vanity and an evil preoccupation.
verses.4:9: Two are better than one, for they have a good reward in their toil.
verses.4:10: For if they fall, the one will raise up his partner; but woe to the one who is alone when he falls and there is no second one to raise him up.
verses.4:11: Moreover, if two lie down, they have warmth; but how shall one alone be warmed?
verses.4:12: And if one grows strong, the two will stand against him; and the threefold cord will not quickly be torn apart.
verses.4:13: Better is a poor and wise youth than an elderly and foolish king, who no longer knows how to take heed.
verses.4:14: For out of the house of prisoners he shall come forth to reign, because even in his kingdom he became poor.
verses.4:15: I saw all the living who walk under the sun with the second young man, who will stand in his place.
verses.4:16: There is no end to all the people, to all those who were before them; yet those who come last will not rejoice in him. For this also is vanity and an inclination of spirit.
verses.4:17: Guard your foot whenever you go to the house of God, and be near to listen; your sacrifice is better than the gift of fools, for they do not know that they do evil.
verses.5:1: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart be quick to utter a word before the face of God; for God is in heaven above, and you are upon the earth; therefore let your words be few.
verses.5:2: For a dream comes in a multitude of trial, and the voice of a fool in a multitude of words.
verses.5:3: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to pay it; there is no delight in fools. Therefore, pay whatever you vow.
verses.5:4: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay.
verses.5:5: Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the face of God, "It is an error," lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
verses.5:6: For in a multitude of dreams and vanities and many words—rather, as for you, fear God.
verses.5:7: If you see the oppression of the poor and the seizure of judgment and righteousness in a province, do not marvel at the matter; for a high one is above a high one to keep watch, and high ones are over them.
verses.5:8: And the abundance of the land—over all is a king of the cultivated field.
verses.5:9: He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; and who has loved yield in their abundance? This also is vanity.
verses.5:10: In an abundance of goodness, those who eat it are multiplied; and what advantage is there for the one who possesses it, since it is only the beginning of seeing with his eye?
verses.5:11: Sweet is the sleep of the servant, whether he eats little or much; but for the one who is filled with riches, there is nothing allowing him to sleep.
verses.5:12: There is a sickness that I have seen under the sun: wealth kept for its owner to his own harm,
verses.5:13: and that wealth will perish in an evil preoccupation; and he fathers a son, yet there is nothing in his hand.
verses.5:14: As he came forth naked from his mother's womb, so he will return to depart just as he came, and he will take nothing from his toil that may go in his hand.
verses.5:15: This also is an evil sickness: for just as he arrived, so also he will depart; and the profit he has, for which he toils, is for the wind.
verses.5:16: Moreover, all his days are in darkness and in mourning, and in much anger and sickness and bitterness.
verses.5:17: Behold, I have seen a good thing that is fitting: to eat and to drink and to see goodness in all his toil with which he toils under the sun, throughout the number of the days of his life that God has given him; for this is his portion.
verses.5:18: Indeed, as for every man to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and granted authority over them to eat of it and to receive his portion and to rejoice in his toil—this is a gift of God.
verses.5:19: For he will not remember other things throughout the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied in the gladness of his heart.
verses.6:1: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it is great under man:
verses.6:2: a man to whom God gives wealth and possessions and honor, and he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God does not grant him power to eat of it, for a stranger eats it. This is vanity and an evil sickness.
verses.6:3: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, however abundant the days of his years may be, yet his soul is not satisfied with goodness, and he has no burial as well, I said, "A stillborn child is better than he."
verses.6:4: For it came in vanity and departs in darkness, and in darkness its name will be covered;
verses.6:5: moreover, it has not seen the sun, nor has it known; yet there is rest for this one rather than for that one.
verses.6:6: Even if he lived the returns of a thousand years and saw no goodness, does he not go to one place?
verses.6:7: All the toil of a man is for his mouth, and yet the soul will not be filled.
verses.6:8: For there is an advantage to the wise man over the fool, because the poor man knows how to walk before life.
verses.6:9: Better is the sight of the eyes than that which wanders with the soul; this also is vanity and an inclination of spirit.
verses.6:10: Whatever has come into being, its name has already been called, and it is known what man is; and he will not be able to contend in judgment with the One who is stronger than he.
verses.6:11: For there are many words that multiply vanity.
verses.6:12: What advantage is there for man? For who knows what is good for man in life, throughout the number of the days of his life of vanity? And he has spent them in a shadow; for who will declare to man what will be after him under the sun?
verses.7:1: A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of birth.
verses.7:2: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of drinking, because this is the end of every man, and the living will lay what is good to his heart.
verses.7:3: Anger is better than laughter, for by sadness of countenance it shall be made better.
verses.7:4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, and the heart of fools is in the house of gladness.
verses.7:5: It is better to hear the rebuke of a wise man than a man who hears the song of fools.
verses.7:6: Like the sound of thorns beneath the cauldron, so is the laughter of fools; and this also is vanity.
verses.7:7: For oppression drives a wise man astray and destroys the heart of his nobility.
verses.7:8: The end of words is better than their beginning; one who is longsuffering is better than one lofty in spirit.
verses.7:9: Do not be hasty in your spirit to grow angry, for anger shall rest in the bosom of fools.
verses.7:10: Do not say, "What has happened that the former days were better than these?" For you have not inquired concerning this in wisdom.
verses.7:11: Wisdom is good along with an inheritance, and an advantage to those who behold the sun;
verses.7:12: for in its shadow wisdom is like the shadow of silver, and the advantage of the knowledge of wisdom shall give life to the one who belongs to it.
verses.7:13: Consider the works of God; for who will be able to set in order him whom God has made crooked?
verses.7:14: In a day of goodness live in good, and consider in a day of adversity. Behold, this also God has made in harmony with that concerning speech, so that man may find nothing after him.
verses.7:15: I have seen all things in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and there is an ungodly man abiding in his wickedness.
verses.7:16: Do not become overly righteous, nor make yourself overly wise, lest you be dismayed.
verses.7:17: Do not act overly ungodly, and do not become hard, lest you die when it is not your time.
verses.7:18: It is good for you to hold fast to this, and indeed from that do not defile your hand; for to those who fear God all things shall come forth.
verses.7:19: Wisdom shall help the wise man more than ten rulers who are in the city;
verses.7:20: for there is no righteous man upon the earth who will do good and will not sin.
verses.7:21: Moreover, do not set your heart upon all the words that the ungodly shall speak, so that you may not hear your servant cursing you;
verses.7:22: for very many times he will deal wickedly with you, and on many occasions he will afflict your heart, because you yourself have likewise cursed others.
verses.7:23: All these things I have tested in wisdom. I said, "I shall be made wise," yet it withdrew far from me,
verses.7:24: farther than what was, and a deep depth—who will find it?
verses.7:25: I turned about, and my heart, to know and to examine and to seek wisdom and the reckoning, and to know the folly of the ungodly, and turmoil and madness;
verses.7:26: and I find it, and I will say, more bitter than death is the woman who is a snare, and her heart is dragnets, a bond upon her hands; he who is good before the face of God shall be delivered from her, but he who sins shall be captured in her.
verses.7:27: "Behold, this I have found," said the Preacher, "one to another, to find the reasoning
verses.7:28: which my soul has earnestly sought, yet I have not found: one man out of a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
verses.7:29: Only behold, this I have found, that God made man upright, yet they have sought out many reasonings." Who knows the wise? And who knows the interpretation of a word?
verses.8:1: The wisdom of a man shall illumine his countenance, and the one who is shameless in his countenance shall be hated.
verses.8:2: Keep the mouth of the king, and concerning the matter of an oath of God
verses.8:3: do not be hasty; you shall depart from his presence; do not stand in an evil matter, for all that he may desire he shall do,
verses.8:4: just as a king who exercises authority; and who shall say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.8:5: He who keeps a commandment will know no evil thing, and the heart of a wise man knows a time of judgment;
verses.8:6: for to every matter there is a time and judgment, because the knowledge of man is great upon him;
verses.8:7: for there is no one who knows what is to come; for how it shall come to pass, who will declare to him?
verses.8:8: There is no man who has authority over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority in the day of death, and there is no discharge in the day of war; neither shall ungodliness deliver the one who belongs to it.
verses.8:9: And all this I saw, and I gave my heart to every work that has been done under the sun, in all the ways that man has ruled over man to harm him;
verses.8:10: and then I saw the ungodly brought into tombs, even from the holy place; and they departed and were praised in the city because they had done thus. This also is vanity.
verses.8:11: Because no contradiction is swiftly made from those who do evil, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.8:12: He who has sinned has done evil from that time and from their long continuance; yet indeed I know that it is good for those who fear God, that they may fear before His face;
verses.8:13: and it shall not be good for the ungodly, neither shall he prolong days in shadow, who does not fear before the face of God.
verses.8:14: There is a vanity that has been done upon the earth, that there are righteous men upon whom it comes like the work of the ungodly, and there are ungodly men to whom it comes like the work of the righteous; I said that this also is vanity.
verses.8:15: And I praised gladness, because there is nothing good for man under the sun except to eat and to drink and to be glad; and this shall abide with him in his toil during the days of his life, as many as God has given him under the sun.
verses.8:16: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the travail that has been done upon the earth, for both by day and by night one does not see sleep with his eyes,
verses.8:17: then I beheld all the works of God, that man will not be able to discover the work that is done under the sun; however much a man may toil to search it out, yet he will not find it; and indeed, though a wise man speak of knowing it, he will not be able to discover it; for all this I laid to my heart, and with my heart I saw all this:
verses.9:1: that the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God; neither love nor hatred does man know; all things are before their face,
verses.9:2: vanity in all things. One event befalls the righteous and the ungodly, the good and the evil, the clean and the unclean, him who sacrifices and him who does not sacrifice. As is the good man, so is the sinner; as is he who swears, so is he who fears an oath.
verses.9:3: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that one event comes to all; moreover, the heart of the sons of men is filled with evil, and madness is in their heart during their life, and after them, to the dead.
verses.9:4: For who is he who shares with all the living? There is hope; for the living dog itself is better than the dead lion.
verses.9:5: For the living will know that they shall die, whereas the dead know nothing at all; neither have they any longer a reward, because their remembrance has been forgotten.
verses.9:6: Indeed, their love, their hatred, and their zeal have already perished, and no longer is there a portion for them forever in all that has been done under the sun.
verses.9:7: Come, eat your bread in gladness, and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already been well pleased with your works.
verses.9:8: At every season let your garments be white, and let oil upon your head not be lacking;
verses.9:9: and behold life with a wife whom you have loved all the days of your life of vanity that have been given to you under the sun. All are the days of your vapor; for that is your portion in your life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
verses.9:10: Everything that your hand may find to do, do according to your strength; for there is no work, nor reasoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Hades, where you are going.
verses.9:11: I turned again and beheld under the sun that the race does not belong to the swift, nor battle to the mighty, neither bread to the wise man, nor wealth to those of understanding, nor favor to those who know; for time and occurrence shall meet all of them.
verses.9:12: For indeed man does not know his season: like the fish that are taken in an evil net, and like birds that are taken in a trap, just like them the sons of men are ensnared in an evil time, when it falls upon them suddenly.
verses.9:13: This wisdom also I saw under the sun, and it is great to me:
verses.9:14: a small city and few men in it, and a great king comes against it and surrounds it and builds great siege works against it,
verses.9:15: and finds in it a poor wise man, and he himself delivers the city by his wisdom—yet no man remembered that poor man.
verses.9:16: Then I said, "Wisdom is better than strength; yet the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded."
verses.9:17: The words of the wise are heard in quietness rather than the outcry of rulers in follies.
verses.9:18: Wisdom is better than instruments of war, yet one sinner shall destroy much goodness.
verses.10:1: Deadly flies will corrupt a preparation, the oil of sweet spice; more precious is the word of wisdom than the glory of great folly.
verses.10:2: The heart of a wise man is toward his right, and the heart of a fool is toward his left.
verses.10:3: Indeed, even when a fool walks along the way, his heart will be lacking, and all that he considers is folly.
verses.10:4: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not forsake your place, for healing will put an end to great sins.
verses.10:5: There is an evil which I saw under the sun, as an unintentional error that went forth from the presence of a ruler.
verses.10:6: The fool was set in great heights, and the rich shall sit in a lowly place.
verses.10:7: I saw servants upon horses, and princes walking like servants upon the earth.
verses.10:8: He who digs a pit shall fall into it, and whoever tears down a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.10:9: He who quarries stones shall be hurt by them; he who splits logs shall be endangered by them.
verses.10:10: If the iron falls off, and he has troubled the face, then he shall strengthen his forces; and the advantage to the man is not wisdom.
verses.10:11: If a serpent bites without a whispered charm, then there is no advantage to the charmer.
verses.10:12: The words of a wise man's mouth are grace, but the lips of a fool shall drown him.
verses.10:13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly, and his end is wicked madness.
verses.10:14: And the fool multiplies words. Man does not know what has been and what shall be; what is after him, who shall declare to him?
verses.10:15: The toil of fools shall afflict them—one who does not know how to go to the city.
verses.10:16: Woe to you, O city, whose king is a youth, and whose princes eat in the morning.
verses.10:17: Blessed are you, O land, whose king is a son of free men, and whose princes shall eat in due season in strength, and shall not be put to shame.
verses.10:18: Through slothfulness the rafters shall be brought low, and through idleness of hands the house shall leak.
verses.10:19: For laughter they make bread, and wine and oil to make the living glad; and in submissiveness all things shall obey silver.
verses.10:20: Do not curse a king even in your conscience, and in the inner recesses of your bedchambers do not curse a rich man; for a bird of the sky shall carry away your voice, and that which has wings shall report your word.
verses.11:1: Send forth your bread upon the face of the water, for in a multitude of days you shall find it.
verses.11:2: Give a portion to seven, and indeed to eight, for you do not know what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.11:3: If the clouds are filled with rain, they pour it out upon the earth; and if a tree falls in the south or in the north, in the place where the tree shall fall, there it shall be.
verses.11:4: He who watches the wind shall not sow, and he who looks at the clouds shall not reap.
verses.11:5: Just as there is no one who knows what is the way of the spirit, like the bones in the womb of her who is with child, so you shall not know the works of God, all things that He shall do.
verses.11:6: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand cease, for you do not know which shall prosper, either this or that, or whether both alike shall be good.
verses.11:7: And sweet is the light, and good it is for the eyes to behold the sun.
verses.11:8: For even if a man lives many years, he shall rejoice in them all, and he shall remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many; all that comes is vanity.
verses.11:9: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth; and walk blameless in the ways, and not in the sight of your eyes; and know that for all these things God shall bring you into judgment.
verses.11:10: And remove wrath from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and folly are vanity.
verses.12:1: And remember Him who created you in the days of your youth, before the days of evil come, and the years arrive in which you shall say, "I have no delight in them";
verses.12:2: before the sun and the light, and the moon and the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.12:3: in the day when the keepers of the house shall be shaken, and the men of strength shall be bent, and the grinding women cease because they have become few, and those who look through the openings shall grow dark;
verses.12:4: and they shall shut the doors in the marketplace at the weakness of the sound of her who grinds, and one shall rise up at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be brought low,
verses.12:5: and they shall look toward the height, and terrors shall be in the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the locust shall grow fat, and the caperberry shall be scattered, because man has gone to his eternal home, and the mourners have gone about in the marketplace;
verses.12:6: before the cord of silver is overturned, and the golden blossom is crushed, and the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel rolls down into the cistern,
verses.12:7: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.12:8: "Vanity of vanities," said the Preacher, "all things are vanity."
verses.12:9: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he also taught knowledge to man, and the ear shall trace out the orderly arrangement of proverbs.
verses.12:10: The Preacher sought diligently to find words of delight, and a writing of uprightness, words of truth.
verses.12:11: The words of the wise are like ox-goads, and like nails firmly planted, those from the collections; they were given from one Shepherd.
verses.12:12: And beyond these, my son, beware of making many books; there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.12:13: Hear the end of the matter, the whole of it: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.
verses.12:14: For God shall bring every work into judgment, along with everything overlooked, whether good or evil.

notes.1:1: Greek Ekklēsiastēs means "one who addresses an assembly" (rendered "the Preacher"); the Greek text also specifies "king of Israel in Jerusalem," whereas the Hebrew reads simply "king in Jerusalem."
notes.1:6: In the Greek text, "rising there, it goes toward the south and circles toward the north" refers to the sun (masculine autos) before the verse turns to the wind (pneuma).
notes.1:14: Greek proairesis pneumatos ("purpose of spirit" or "choosing of spirit") renders the Hebrew phrase often translated "grasping for the wind." Here and elsewhere (e.g., 2:17; 3:10, 17), Greek syn mechanically reflects the Hebrew direct-object marker and is left untranslated.
notes.1:17: The Greek text reads "parables and understanding" (parabolas kai epistēmēn) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "madness and folly."
notes.1:18: The Greek text reads "abundance of knowledge" (plēthos gnōseōs) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "much grief" or "vexation."
notes.2:3: The Greek text reads "draw my flesh like wine" (hōs oinon) and "lay hold upon gladness" (ep' euphrosynē), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "with wine" and "lay hold on folly."
notes.2:8: Greek oinochoon kai oinochoas ("a male cupbearer and female cupbearers") translates an obscure Hebrew expression often rendered "concubines" or "musical instruments."
notes.2:12: The Greek reads "after counsel" (opisō tēs boulēs), interpreting the underlying consonants as Aramaic "counsel" rather than Hebrew "the king."
notes.2:15: The closing clause, "because the fool speaks out of abundance," is an explanatory addition distinctive to the Greek Septuagint.
notes.2:24: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat..."), the Greek states that a man possesses no such good of himself, for it comes from the hand of God.
notes.3:2: Greek tou tekein is active ("to give birth") rather than passive ("to be born"). In 3:1-8, the Greek distinguishes chronos ("time," 3:1) from kairos ("season" or appointed moment, 3:1-8).
notes.3:11: Greek ton aiōna ("all eternity" or "the whole age") renders Hebrew ha-olam, which can signify either eternity or the world.
notes.3:15: Greek ton diōkomenon ("the one who is pursued" or "the persecuted one") is masculine personal, whereas the Hebrew is often taken neutrally as "what has passed."
notes.3:16: The Greek reads "there was the godly one" (ho eusebēs) in the place of the righteous, in contrast to the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "there was wickedness."
notes.4:4: The Greek phrase "inclination of spirit" (proairesis pneumatos, literally "choice" or "purpose of spirit") is the Septuagint's characteristic rendering of the Hebrew idiom often translated "striving after wind."
notes.4:17: In the Septuagint, this verse concludes chapter 4 (corresponding to 5:1 in the Hebrew) and reads "your sacrifice is better than the gift of fools," whereas the Hebrew compares drawing near to listen with the sacrifice offered by fools.
notes.5:2: The Greek text reads "trial" (peirasmos) rather than "business" or "preoccupation" as in the Hebrew.
notes.5:5: The Greek text reads "before the face of God" where the Hebrew text reads "before the messenger."
notes.5:10: The Greek phrase "the beginning of seeing" (arche tou horan) reflects a distinctive Septuagint rendering where the Hebrew reads "except to look upon it."
notes.5:16: The Greek text reads "in darkness and in mourning" (en penthei), whereas the Hebrew text reads "in darkness he eats."
notes.5:19: The Greek text reads "not other things" (ouk alla), where the Hebrew text reads "not much."
notes.6:1: The Greek text reads "under man" (hypo ton anthropon), echoing "under the sun," whereas the Hebrew reads "upon man."
notes.6:6: The Greek phrase "the returns of a thousand years" (chilion eton kathodous, also meaning "courses" or "descents") corresponds to the Hebrew "a thousand years twice."
notes.6:8: Whereas the Hebrew frames this verse as two rhetorical questions, the Greek renders it as a declarative statement and reads "before life" (tes zoes) rather than "before the living."
notes.6:12: In the Greek versification, "What advantage is there for man?" opens verse 12 (closing verse 11 in the Hebrew), and "in a shadow" (en skia) appears where the Hebrew has "like a shadow."
notes.7:7: The Greek reads 'the heart of his nobility' (εὐγενείας αὐτοῦ), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'a bribe destroys the heart.'
notes.7:14: The phrase 'concerning speech' (περὶ λαλιᾶς) is a literal Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew idiom meaning 'to the end that / so that.'
notes.7:18: The Greek reads 'do not defile your hand' (μὴ μιάνῃς), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'do not withdraw your hand.'
notes.7:22: The Greek reads 'he will deal wickedly with you... and afflict your heart,' reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text's 'your heart knows.'
notes.7:29: The final two questions correspond to the opening of Ecclesiastes 8:1 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and the Greek asks 'Who knows the wise?' rather than 'Who is like the wise?'
notes.8:1: The Greek reads 'shall be hated' (μισηθήσεται), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew verb than the Masoretic Text's 'is changed.'
notes.8:6: The Greek reads 'the knowledge of man' (γνῶσις), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'the misery/evil of man' through a Hebrew consonant interchange.
notes.8:10: The Greek reads 'and were praised' (ἐπῃνέθησαν), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'and were forgotten.'
notes.8:17: The closing clause ('for all this I laid to my heart, and with my heart I saw all this') corresponds to the opening of Ecclesiastes 9:1 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:2: The opening words 'vanity in all things' (ματαιότης ἐν τοῖς πᾶσιν) reflect a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'all things are alike to all'; the Greek also includes 'and the evil.'
notes.9:9: The Greek shifts from 'vanity' (ματαιότητος) in the first clause to 'vapor' (ἀτμοῦ) in 'All are the days of your vapor.'
notes.9:10: Greek ᾅδῃ ('Hades') is the standard Septuagint rendering of Hebrew Sheol, the realm of the dead.
notes.9:17: The Greek reads plural 'rulers in follies' (ἐξουσιαζόντων ἐν ἀφροσύναις) rather than the singular 'a ruler among fools' found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:1: The Greek text reads "more precious is the word of wisdom than the glory of great folly," diverging markedly from the Masoretic Hebrew ("a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor").
notes.10:10: The Greek diverges from the Hebrew, speaking of the iron falling off and ending literally "and the advantage to the man is not wisdom" (some Greek manuscripts read "to the valiant man is wisdom").
notes.10:17: The Greek reads "and shall not be put to shame," whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "and not for drunkenness."
notes.10:19: The Greek adds "and oil," and the phrase "in submissiveness... shall obey" reflects a double rendering of the Hebrew verb root that can mean either "humble" or "answer."
notes.11:5: Greek pneuma can mean either "spirit" or "wind," and the Greek uses an impersonal construction ("there is no one who knows") rather than the second-person verb of the Hebrew.
notes.11:9: The Greek reads "walk blameless in the ways, and not in the sight of your eyes," a distinctive Septuagint reading differing from the Masoretic Hebrew ("walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes").
notes.11:10: The Greek pairs youth with "folly" (anoia), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew has a rare word usually rendered "prime of life" or "dark hair."
notes.12:5: The Greek reads "they shall look toward the height" (rather than fearing heights), "the locust shall grow fat," and explicitly names the "caperberry" (kapparis).
notes.12:6: Greek anthemion refers to a golden floral ornament or blossom-shaped bowl, and anatrape literally means "is overturned."
notes.12:9: The Greek reads "man" (rather than "the people") and "the ear shall trace out the orderly arrangement of proverbs," taking the Hebrew verb for pondering as the noun "ear."
notes.12:14: Greek pareoramenon means "overlooked" or "passed over," corresponding to "hidden" or "secret" in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
